title: Maple Syrup Custard Ice Cream
changes_from_base: Reduced maple syrup sweetens it on its own; no sugar or vanilla.
summary: Our classic custard ice cream sweetened only with maple syrup, reduced first for a deeper, almost toffee-like flavour. No sugar or vanilla needed.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Reduce the syrup
steps.text: Simmer the maple syrup in the saucepan for 4-5 min until reduced to about 180 ml. Concentrating it intensifies the flavour without the thin, watery result of using more syrup.

steps.title: Add the dairy
steps.text: Off the heat, whisk in the milk carefully, as it will sputter, then the cream. Warm over medium heat until steaming.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Whisk the yolks in the heatproof bowl, add two ladles of the maple dairy while whisking and pour back into the pan.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Stir over low heat until the custard coats the spatula and reads 77-80 °C. Hold it below a simmer to keep it silky.

steps.title: Chill thoroughly
steps.text: Stir in the salt, sieve, cool over the iced water and refrigerate for at least 6 h. Syrup-sweetened bases benefit from a longer rest.

steps.title: Churn and freeze
steps.text: Churn until thick, then freeze for at least 4 h. It stays a little softer than sugar-based ice cream, so it scoops easily.

tips: Choose a dark, robust maple syrup for the strongest flavour; never use maple-flavoured pancake syrup.
A common mistake is walking away from the reducing syrup; it can foam over in seconds. Use a deep pan and stay close.
A sprinkle of toasted pecans is excellent on top.
storage: Keep frozen in a covered container for up to 2 weeks.
